lines.line: *Note: This opening is from the traditional Tamil verse (Thiruppavai / Divya Prabandham style praise).*

details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Kondhal (Cloud-like) | Vannanai (one with the color/complexion) | Kovalanaai (as the cowherd / protector)
Literal translation: "The cloud-complexioned cowherd."
Translation: "The one who has the dark hue of rain clouds, the divine cowherd."
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Vennai (butter) | Unda (who ate) | Va (mouth) | Yennin (my) | Ullam (heart/mind) | Kavarthanae (stole / captivated)
Literal translation: "The mouth that ate butter captivated my heart."
Translation: "The one who ate butter with that sweet mouth has completely stolen my heart."
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Anda (universe/cosmic) | Kula (family/lineage) | Ne (you) | Arandha (limitless/divine) | Nin (your) | Amudinai (sweet nectar)
Literal translation: "You, of the cosmic lineage, your limitless nectar."
Translation: "You, ruler of the universe, your limitless divine sweetness."
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Kanda (having seen) | Kangal (eyes) | Mai (other / illusion) | Thonrinai (manifestation) | Kaanathey (will not look at)
Literal translation: "Eyes having seen this will not see anything else."
Translation: "Having beheld your beauty, these eyes cannot look at anything else."

lines.line: **Ban ke titli dil udaa udaa udaa hai kaheen door**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Ban ke (becoming / like) | titli (butterfly) | dil (heart) | udaa (flew / flying) | hai (is) | kaheen door (somewhere far away)
Literal translation: "Becoming a butterfly, heart has flown far away somewhere."
Translation: "Like a butterfly, my heart has flown off somewhere far away."

lines.line: **Chal ke khushboo se judaa judaa judaa hai kahin door**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Chal ke (walking / leaving) | khushboo se (from fragrance) | judaa (separated / adrift) | hai (is) | kahin door (somewhere far away)
Literal translation: "Walking away, detached from fragrance, somewhere far."
Translation: "Drifting along, trailing like fragrance to a distant place."
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Haadse (events / incidents) | ye (these) | kaise (how / what kind of) | ansune (unheard of) | se (like) | jaise (as if)
Literal translation: "What incidents are these, unheard of as if."
Translation: "What kind of unexpected moments are these—unheard of and surreal."
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Choome (kisses) | andheron ko (to the darknesses) | koi (some / a) | noor (divine light / glow)
Literal translation: "Some radiant light kisses the dark."
Translation: "As if a radiant beam of light just kissed the darkness."

lines.line: **Sirf keh jaaun yaa aasmaan pe likh doon**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Sirf (just / only) | keh jaaun (should I just say) | yaa (or) | aasmaan pe (on the sky) | likh doon (should I write)
Literal translation: "Should I just say it or should I write on the sky."
Translation: "Should I merely say it aloud, or paint it across the sky?"
Word-by-word breakdown into English: Teree (your) | taareefon mein (in praises) | chashme baddoor (ward off the evil eye / touch wood)
Literal translation: "In your praises, may evil eyes stay away."
Translation: "In praise of your beauty—may no evil eye ever touch you!"

lines.line: **Bhoori Bhoori, Aankhein Teri, Kanakhiyon Se Tez Teer Kitne Chhode**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Bhoori bhoori (hazel / brown) | aankhein teri (your eyes) | kanakhiyon se (from sidelong glances) | tez teer (sharp arrows) | kitne (so many) | chhode (shot / released)
Literal translation: "Your brown eyes shot how many sharp arrows from side glances."
Translation: "Those brown eyes of yours have shot so many sharp arrows from their sidelong glances."

lines.line: **Dhaani Dhaani, Baatein Teri, Udte Phirte Panchhiyon Ke Rukh Bhi Mode**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Dhaani dhaani (light-green / fresh / tender) | baatein teri (your words / talks) | udte phirte (flying around) | panchhiyon ke (of the birds) | rukh (direction) | bhi (even) | mode (turned)
Literal translation: "Your fresh sweet words turned even flying birds' directions."
Translation: "Your soothing, fresh words can turn the course of birds in mid-flight."

lines.line: **Adhoori Thi Zara Si, Main Poori Ho Rahi Hoon, Teri Saadgi Mein Hoke Choor**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Adhoori (incomplete) | thi (was) | zara si (a little bit) | main (I) | poori ho rahi hoon (am becoming complete) | teri (your) | saadgi mein (in simplicity) | hoke choor (becoming immersed / overwhelmed)
Literal translation: "I was a little incomplete, I am becoming whole, lost completely in your simplicity."
Translation: "I was somewhat incomplete, but now I feel whole, completely taken by your simplicity."

lines.line: **Raatein Gin Ke, Neendein Bun Ke, Cheez Kya Hai, Khwaabdaari Humne Jaani**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Raatein gin ke (counting nights) | neendein bun ke (weaving sleep/dreams) | cheez kya hai (what kind of thing it is) | khwaabdaari (dreaming / keeping dreams) | humne jaani (we learned / understood)
Literal translation: "Counting nights, weaving sleep, what dreams are we came to know."
Translation: "Counting the nights and weaving dreams, I finally learned what it truly means to dream."

lines.line: **Tere Sur Ka, Saaz Banke, Hote Kya Hain Raagdaari Humne Jaani**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Tere sur ka (of your melody) | saaz banke (becoming the instrument) | hote kya hain (what are) | raagdaari (classical melody / harmony) | humne jaani (we came to know)
Literal translation: "Becoming instrument of your musical note, what melody is we came to know."
Translation: "Becoming an instrument to your melody, I discovered what true harmony is."

lines.line: **Jo Dil Ko Bha Rahi Hai Woh Teri Shayari Hai, Ya Koi Shayarana Hai Fitoor**
details: Word-by-word breakdown into English: Jo (that which) | dil ko (to the heart) | bha rahi hai (is pleasing / appealing) | woh (that) | teri (your) | shayari (poetry) | hai (is) | ya (or) | koi (some) | shayarana (poetic) | hai (is) | fitoor (obsession / passion)
Literal translation: "What pleases the heart is that your poetry, or some poetic obsession."
Translation: "Is this sweet feeling your poetry winning over my heart, or just a poetic madness of love?"
